The headlining film is a Billie Eilish 3D concert experience co-directed by James Cameron.

Recent findings suggest that meta has rolled out 3D movie rentals for its headsets. Users can now rent or buy films through the TV app on both the Meta Quest 3 and Meta Quest 3S.

The lineup of available titles is topped by HIT ME HARD AND SOFT: THE TOUR (LIVE IN 3D). Meta Quest will be the exclusive host for the 3D version of the Billie Eilish concert movie until December 31. The project is a big budget affair co-directed by the pop artist and James Cameron. It was shot with a custom system for 3D filming at range so that the show's live audience wouldn't be interrupted by cameras and the at-home viewers could still experience the sensation of being onstage along with Eilish.

It has been revealed that earlier this month, Disney began making its library of 3D films available on Meta Quest via the Disney+ app. Having more media embrace the tech is a welcome addition for fans of 3D (although it may have felt like an unnecessarily long wait). But today's announcement includes a note from Meta that the TV app will continue adding more content, including "thousands of titles and international availability coming with the launch of Meta VR Glasses in spring 2027.".

Industry News: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm vendor hacks as n0n leaks customer data

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • JPMorgan Chase indicates hackers got into data held by companies that work for the bank, and that it may include some customers’ names and email addresses.
  • We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.
  • Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JPMorgan Chase indicates hackers got into data held by companies that work for the bank, and that it may include some customers’ names and email addresses. Visa and Mastercard have also confirmed incidents at outside providers.

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

There is no disruption to our services.

Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring.

There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.

— Chase (@Chase) November 19, 2026.

The bank stated the attackers accessed marketing data held by those vendors. Its own services kept running. It will offer affected customers free credit monitoring where appropriate.

Chase also remarked the attack has no link to Monday’s outage, which it blamed on a software bug in its own hardware.

Sources indicate that A ransomware gang called n0n published the data after a 48-hour deadline passed, Cybernews reported. Its researchers found about 16,000 customer email addresses, Chase account IDs and, in some cases, phone numbers. The file also holds 124 email addresses of bank staff.

All of the records seem to relate to Chase’s Reserve card, Cybernews stated. The invitation-only Visa card is for wealthy clients, usually with at least $10m in managed assets.

“This association alone makes the leak a lot more sensitive,” mentioned Aras Nazarovas, a senior security researcher at Cybernews.

Recent findings suggest that the file is only 502KB. It is not clear whether it is a sample or all the gang took. TNW has not independently verified the data.

Sources indicate that A Mastercard spokesperson told Business Insider that an outside provider exposed a limited number of email addresses. They belong to a small group of cardholders in one benefit programme. Mastercard said it has contained the exposure.

“There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards,” the spokesperson said.

Visa stated its incident involved a service provider in the Asia Pacific region.

“Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected,” a Visa spokesperson stated.

None of the three companies has named the vendors or said how many customers the breach hit.

Sources indicate that n0n is a new gang, first tracked in mid-September, according to Cybernews. Last week it claimed to have stolen data from Expedia.

According to recent reports, the leak comes at the end of a week of outages across the US. Wall Street executives and the NSA have reportedly blamed several of them on rushed security patches for flaws that AI found, not on hackers. Earlier this week, attackers also used Optimizely’s testing tool to plant malware on major websites.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI gadget was revealed in September as a standalone way to interact with the manufacturer’s AI agent.

Meta reportedly plans to sell the Muse Charm, a Tamagotchi-esque gadget for talking to its Muse AI agent, for $300, according to The Information. The manufacturer introduced the Muse Charm at Meta Connect in September as a way to use its agent without having to reach for a smartphone, and said it would launch in time for the holidays.

At Connect, CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted the Muse Charm packs "the whole Muse experience, including the real-time voice and avatar stack into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to." The device features a fingerprint reader to verify your identity before you're able to give commands and will come with up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon, The Information reports.

Engadget has asked Meta to comment on The Information's report. We'll upgrade this article if we hear back.

In October, Meta shared open source guides for interested developers to build their own "Muse Gadgets." The company is clearly trying to capitalize on the popularity of Muse — the agent has already drawn more than 10 million consumers — by making it as accessible as possible and leaning into the cuteness and customizability of the Muse avatar. The company also recently released a Muse app for Wear OS and watchOS. Meta's work on its own smartwatch-like device has been delayed to 2027, according to The Information.

Meta's larger goal for its AI models and hardware products appears to be directly owning its relationship with customers. Right now most people access Meta's products through apps on their smartphones, where they're subject to Apple's and Google's rules. A world where an AI agent takes the place of a variety of apps and is usable without a phone is one where Meta has a lot more control. The tech giant is also working on commerce tools that will allow it to charge businesses a fee when Muse owners make a purchase via the agent. Mark Zuckerberg has noted he believes Muse could one day generate more revenue per user than the company's existing apps.

Latest Update: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense firm, feds say

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.
  • Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the manufacturer’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday.
  • “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the manufacturer’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”.

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”.

When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly noted he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”.

In a recent development, prosecutors didn’t name the company, but both Reuters and Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully in the summer of 2026 after being recruited by someone over Telegram. Prosecutors stated the party gave D’iu a clandestine assignment to target employees of a large technology and defense company. D’iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support along with information that his work was on behalf of “the motherland.” His instructions were to collect information about the company because it was supplying weapons for use against Russian forces in Ukraine.

Prosecutors mentioned D’iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City in June. He then crossed the border into the US and was instructed to buy laptops, cell phones, wireless networking equipment, and remote access software. Besides instructions to monitor tech giant employees at the coffee shop, D’iu’s orders also included positioning his laptop at certain locations near the company so it could be remotely accessed in an attempt to collect information from company employees nearby.

D’iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity as he conducted his activities. The documents included a falsified California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of “Hugo Landry Johns.” The passport was allegedly an authentic US passport that originally had been issued to someone elsewhere in the country. It was modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

Sources indicate that D’iu was arrested on October 30 and remains in custody. He is charged with one count of Conspiracy to Act as an Agent of a Foreign Government, one count of Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, and one count of Interstate Stalking. If convicted for Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release. He faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release for each conviction on the other two charges.

Recent findings suggest that D’iu had his initial appearance in federal court on November 2. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

Industry News: Anthropic rival notes companies can (mostly) skip the pricey models

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1217 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.
  • That’s the enormous opportunity being chased by companies like Fireworks AI, as enterprises seek ways to avoid paying frontier prices for their AI needs.
  • Fireworks runs AI models for other businesses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.

That’s the enormous opportunity being chased by companies like Fireworks AI, as enterprises seek ways to avoid paying frontier prices for their AI needs.

Fireworks runs AI models for other businesses. It specializes in open-weight models, which anyone can download, and helps customers tune them on their own data so they run faster and cheaper than the models of Anthropic, OpenAI, and other heavyweights, and are harder for rivals to copy. Customers have included Uber, Shopify, and Notion. Co-founder Chenyu Zhao and I spoke onstage toward the end of the day.

Industry observers note that zhao and many others believe companies are gravitating toward platforms like his because frontier models are pricey and, in most cases, he says, unnecessary unless you need the very latest and greatest generalized intelligence. There are also growing concerns that frontier labs absorb too much of their customers’ know-how, even if only through the prompts used to get answers, a worry Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella raised in July.

Fireworks has also gotten its first black eye, having disclosed two security incidents this fall. In one, hackers reached API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts; in the other, attackers breached its cloud provider, made their way into a development system, and nabbed customer data, including billing records and some datasets.

It has been revealed that notion claims AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of its workspaces were exposed, but it has disconnected from Fireworks. Uber says hackers stole the names, addresses, birth dates and driver’s license numbers of about 150,000 drivers through a vendor that TechCrunch identified as Fireworks. Fireworks will have to win back the confidence of customers like them.

Fireworks, assigned a $17.5 billion valuation by its investors in summer, is reportedly in “early talks” for yet another round, though Zhao declined to comment.

Recent findings suggest that there’s money chasing everyone in the category, seems like. Rival companies Together AI and Baseten have confirmed massive rounds in recent months. On Wednesday, Palo Alto Networks remarked it will buy Applied Compute, which, like Fireworks, helps companies train and run custom AI models on their own data. The deal for the startup, founded just a year ago by former OpenAI researchers, is $4.5 billion, all of it in stock.

Recent findings suggest that here’s some of what Zhao had to say. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

Industry observers note that you spent a decade at Google, including managing a 50-person engineering team on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Why leave when you did?

When you meet great co-founders, it’s obvious within five minutes that they’re really smart. I was sold after talking to Lin [Qiao] and Dima [Dzhulgakov]. It’s also crucial to find people who are genuinely nice, people you’ll enjoy working with.

How do you describe Fireworks to a CEO who has never heard of it?

I describe Fireworks as a specialized intelligence platform. OpenAI and Anthropic are building general intelligence. We use open models, which are often smaller, cheaper, and faster, and let companies add their own data to specialize them. That way you own your AI rather than being beholden to giant AI conglomerates. If you’re just using Opus or Sonnet, that’s not a differentiator.

How far behind are open models right now?

It has been revealed that A few years ago I’d have remarked a year, a year and a half. Then came DeepSeek and a waterfall of fantastic open models. These days it’s at most six months behind, probably closer to three.

If the models are so close behind, why are businesses slow to switch?

Frontier models are a household brand, and before you find product-market fit, using the best model is low risk. But once you pass 10,000 or 100,000 owners and you’re spending $10,000 to $100,000 a month on tokens, it’s time to think about open source.

In July, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that companies using proprietary AI models pay twice, once in money and again in know-how. Do you think that warning had a material effect?

We think we’ll live in a two-model world, with frontier and open models in parallel. You want the best intelligence for high-level planning, but you don’t need a frontier model for basic arithmetic. That’s why there’s so much interest in routing, and why people now think about cost per task, not just cost per token.

Anthropic went public today. What do you think of its valuation? There’s one scenario in which it just continues to cement its place in this sort of oligopoly; there’s another where it starts to lose traction.

According to recent reports, on the record: I’ll probably call my broker tonight and buy a few shares. This is a long-term bet. In 10 years AI usage will be at a completely different scale, and that takes an incredible amount of capital, which is why these companies are going public.

Fireworks has had a couple of security breaches recently. What do you tell customers?

Every company is probably seeing an unprecedented frequency of attacks. For our incident, a lot of the motivation was LLM jacking: hunting through providers for API keys and secrets to sell tokens on illicit marketplaces. Our promise is zero data retention for inference traffic, and there’s no indication that has been compromised.

Recent findings suggest that notion has disconnected from Fireworks. Did you lose other customers?

According to recent reports, I don’t think I can publicly name the specific customers that were impacted. Some, such as Notion and Cursor, have gone public already. It was a small subset of our customers that had this data impact.

How did that customer data get exposed, given your zero-retention promise?

Sources indicate that notion was using batch prediction, where you upload a dataset that’s stored at rest, so it’s not a zero-retention product by nature. We’re moving those services to an online flow so we keep data only as long as we need it.

Jensen Huang left Nvidia last week, and Nvidia has backed Fireworks since 2024. Does that affect you?

It’s been a blow to the industry, and we feel for Jensen and his family. But Nvidia has always been a strong supporter of open source, and I don’t see that changing. We expect it to keep investing in Nemotron, and we’re excited to keep partnering with them.

Magnific passes $300M ARR and may raise outside money next year

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Magnific, the Spanish AI creative platform once called Freepik, has not raised a funding round since 2010.
  • “On outside investment, we have no looks today, but nothing is set in stone.
  • Magnific stated on Tuesday that it has passed $300M in annual recurring revenue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joaquín Cuenca, co-founder and CEO of Magnific.

Magnific, the Spanish AI creative platform once called Freepik, has not raised a funding round since 2010. Its customers have paid for everything, including the move into AI, co-founder and chief executive Joaquín Cuenca told TNW.

“On outside investment, we have no looks today, but nothing is set in stone. The investment this market requires is very significant, and if taking capital lets us accelerate, it may happen, maybe next year,” Cuenca mentioned.

Magnific stated on Tuesday that it has passed $300M in annual recurring revenue. It had $230M when it rebranded from Freepik in April. It is opening offices in Shanghai and Singapore and will spend $10M in Asia Pacific through early 2027.

It has been revealed that magnific says that makes it Europe’s fourth-largest generative AI company by ARR, on publicly reported figures. Only Lovable, ElevenLabs and Mistral rank higher. Mistral raised €3bn in September, and ElevenLabs doubled its valuation to $22bn in a share sale.

It has been revealed that magnific is still bootstrapped, Cuenca said. EQT took a majority stake in 2020. It bought shares from his partners and never put new money into the firm.

Magnific is EBITDA positive, he remarked. Profit is thinner than revenue suggests, because most of the money goes straight back into AI compute. Every time a better image or video model comes out, people want it that same day, he added.

“We already spend hundreds of millions of dollars generating what our consumers ask for,” Cuenca remarked.

An IPO is not on the table today, Cuenca remarked. Public markets now ask for far bigger companies than they used to. His target is to pass $1bn in revenue by the end of next year. He expects to get there organically.

“What I value is that there is no timer on us,” Cuenca noted.

According to recent reports, several of the best video models are Chinese, and users pick them because they win on quality, Cuenca said. Magnific runs ByteDance’s Seedance, Kuaishou’s Kling, Alibaba’s Wan and MiniMax’s models today.

In a recent development, until last year he had never been to China, and Magnific’s suppliers were American. He has been several times since, once for just 20 hours. China entered Magnific’s top 10 markets this year for the first time.

Magnific is not trying to build its own foundation model to take on Google, ByteDance or OpenAI, Cuenca said. For an independent company, he called that “a lost battle”.

“Think of a MacBook: the models are the CPU, and we build the rest of the machine, the tools, the workflows, the controls,” Cuenca mentioned.

The Shanghai office puts Magnific next to the teams that build those models, he remarked, so it can add new ones faster and pass on feedback from its customers. According to the release, Singapore will be its sales base in the region, alongside existing teams in South Korea, Japan and Thailand.

“Studios need legal guarantees before they use anything in production, and meeting that bar is one of the reasons we are growing with them,” Cuenca mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that magnific’s Enterprise prepares include indemnification against third-party IP claims on what the platform produces, Cuenca said. Customers own what they create, and Magnific does not use their inputs or outputs to train models, he said.

“The exception is bad faith: if you ask for Mickey Mouse and you get Mickey Mouse, that’s on you,” he noted.

According to recent reports, in his view, responsibility has to move to the output. AI can infringe without the user meaning to, so what matters is detecting it and flagging it to the user.

“With any tool you can infringe: if you can draw two overlapping circles, you can infringe Mastercard’s trademark,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that in Singapore, Hagia Labs made the films for telco StarHub’s Unlimited+ Looks campaign, with its creative partner Superson. StarHub’s green characters, the Hublings, fly across Asia and land in Japan. Hagia built the characters and settings in Magnific’s Spaces tool. Done the conventional way, Cuenca remarked, that would have meant travel, crews and a shoot in every location.

According to recent reports, by Hagia’s own estimate, it took two to four weeks from brief to delivery. A conventional shoot would take two to four months.

Recent findings suggest that teams start by doing the same work faster, Cuenca stated. Then they make what they could not afford before. Brands that used to advertise with a still image and a line of copy now make film-quality spots, and studios are greenlighting fantasy and historical projects that used to die on budget.

Recent findings suggest that the next step is automation, he said. A team builds a workflow once in Spaces, and staff or their agents in ChatGPT or Claude can run it through Magnific’s MCP server.

Enterprise adoption in the region grew 35%, which is why Magnific is hiring there instead of flying people in from Málaga, Cuenca noted. The release indicates Magnific looks more than 20 staff in Asia Pacific by the end of 2026, and twice that in 2027. Product and engineering stay at its Málaga headquarters. Cuenca called the offices “a long-term commitment to Asia” in Magnific’s release.

“Being funded by customers forces a discipline I don’t want to lose: you only build what people will pay for,” Cuenca mentioned.

Latest Update: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report indicates

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals.
  • The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.
  • The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA’s own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group’s priority was ever winning elections in the first place.

The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.

The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms. In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously.

According to Stat’s findings, of the $10.5 million the MAHA PAC spent on the midterms, less than a tenth—roughly $1 million—went to messaging on political candidates, which are expenses called “independent expenditures.”.

Andrew Mayersohn, a committees researcher at OpenSecrets, called the spending “pretty unusual,” explaining that “Major super PACs spend most of their money on independent expenditures.”.

Recent findings suggest that in some cases, the scant political spending was dwarfed by spending on luxuries. For instance, in a key House race in Northern California, MAHA supported Kevin Kiley over his political rival, pediatrician Richard Pan. Despite calling the race “the most direct ideological confrontation” between MAHA and its opposition “anywhere on the 2026 ballot,” the PAC only spent $49,900 to back Kiley. That’s a little less than the $50,100 it spent at Mastro’s Steakhouse, an upscale restaurant that offers $110 porterhouse steaks in Washington, DC. Further, it’s less than a third of the $155,900 the PAC spent at Ned’s Club, a luxury club near the White House that has become a popular gathering spot among Trump officials.

Kiley lost the election to Pan by double digits.

Of the roughly $1 million spent on political candidates, most of it—over $700,000—went to defeating Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.). Many other MAHA-endorsed candidates received $50,000 or less. Some got less than $2,000.

In a recent development, outside of steaks and a private club, the MAHA PAC spent $500,000 on a media company, Merit Street Media, run by Phil McGraw, who hosted a MAHA special featuring Dr. Phil. MAHA leaders used PAC money to cover meals, payroll, and credit card bills. The PAC paid $275,000 to a security firm, Gavin de Becker & Associates, which is led by an ally of anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., MAHA’s top leader. Tens of thousands more went to LLCs that have little to no online information.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, prominent online MAHA influencers also pocketed tens of thousands from the PAC, as did writers for The MAHA Report, a Substack that promotes Kennedy and MAHA interests. In the days after the midterms, as members of the movement were coming to grips with the election losses, The MAHA Report chose to publish a lengthy article defending convicted rapist Russel Brand, a Kennedy ally who became a MAHA fixture.

The biggest chunk of the MAHA PAC’s spending—more than $3 million—went to the nonprofit MAHA Action, which is also run by Lyons. It’s unclear how all that money was spent.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (634 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

The GTA 6 star system claims a lot more than just your Wanted level

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, rockstar Games' first gameplay trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 from August suggested the developer had tinkered with some of the core mechanics of the series, including Wanted levels.
  • Recent findings suggest that some of this is thanks to the game's newly introduced concept of Heat, pieces of information the police learn about the player characters that can linger even after your Wanted level lowers.
  • The most obvious visual difference between GTA 6 and GTA 5 is the reintroduction of a sixth Wanted level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, rockstar Games' first gameplay trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 from August suggested the developer had tinkered with some of the core mechanics of the series, including Wanted levels. Now that GTA 6 is out, we have a much better sense of how much has actually changed. While your Wanted level has always been able to communicate a sense of how many police officers are looking for you and how intently they're looking, the updated system also bakes in a lot more detail about what police actively know about protagonists Jason and Lucia.

Recent findings suggest that some of this is thanks to the game's newly introduced concept of Heat, pieces of information the police learn about the player characters that can linger even after your Wanted level lowers. But the visual changes to the Wanted system's iconic star ratings convey nearly as much. Here's how Rockstar's approach to Wanted levels has changed in Grand Theft Auto VI.

The most obvious visual difference between GTA 6 and GTA 5 is the reintroduction of a sixth Wanted level. In the last Grand Theft Auto, your Wanted level maxed out at five stars. As Rockstar teased during its gameplay trailer, GTA 6 caps out at six stars. This is a return to the rating system of older games, going as far back as Grand Theft Auto III — or even further if you consider the "police heads" top-down GTA games used to communicate police response.

As in past games, the number of stars lets you know how hard the police are looking for you. One star could just be a few cops tailing you, while a full six stars indicates a dramatic, militarized response. Besides being a throwback, opting for six stars seems like it allows Rockstar to offer some nuance and variety to the series' classic chase experience. You might eventually get bored if every bank robbery devolves into a helicopter chase.

Industry observers note that just committing a robbery doesn't necessarily mean your Wanted level will rise, either. According to IGN's hands-on demo and interview with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson, crimes need to actually be reported to police to provoke a response. "The Wanted system in GTA 6 requires that someone witness the crime, or an alarm needs to be set off for it to be reported to the law," Nelson told IGN. "Our dispatch is extremely specific in what it knows.".

It has been revealed that once you are "wanted" for a crime, GTA 6 offers a lot more visual information to tell you what police currently know and nudge you toward escaping their scrutiny. Those include icons for the different kinds of information the police know about you as part of the Heat system, and also different treatments of your Wanted level star rating.

When police have direct line of sight with you, your stars are solid white, according to GameSpot, and only start flashing white once you've broken line of sight. Meanwhile, your stars turn red when you're near a crime scene but the police don't know where you are or hollow white when the police are looking for you but have no idea what you look like.

At the same time, some information about the police is also obstructed. GameSpot reports you won't be able to see the police on your minimap, which makes it harder to proposal escape routes in advance. It also notes once you do reach a six-star Wanted level, you'll be pursued throughout the game map, making clean exits more difficult. All of these changes seem like they'll make the fundamental cops-and-robbers gameplay of Grand Theft Auto 6 more engaging. Or at the very least, different from what people have come to expect from the series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.

Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

“We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, mentioned Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip firm’s third quarter earnings call.

In a recent development, by Thursday, the manufacturer’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected.

Recent findings suggest that looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in firm history,” Kress told investors.

Industry observers note that “Our momentum is real,” Kress said. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.”.

But investors are stilltrying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future.

It has been revealed that the firm’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The New York Times.

Recent findings suggest that harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession blueprint — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on.

It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia.

Sources indicate that on October 29th, The Fresh York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center organization and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.”.

In a recent development, nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June.

The stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the upcoming class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64.

Then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a organization-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang remarked he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025.

The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia declared Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the company’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year.

On December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd.

Retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research.

Nvidia’s average price target is $232.59, with the lowest estimate at $130 and the highest at $350, according to an analysis of analyst projections over the last three months by Google Finance.

Industry observers note that nearly two-thirds of those analysts issued a “Buy” rating for Nvidia in the last three months. Of those, all 30 reiterated that rating post-earnings.

The stock closed at $145.98 on Thursday, a upcoming 52-week low.

Then again, numbers are the core basis for stock market ratings, and numbers may not be Nvidia’s problem right now. It’s everything else — the leadership vacuum, upcoming congressional testimony, regulatory uncertainty, broader questions about neocloud customer financing and sales to China — that will continue to impact the stock in the coming weeks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that anthropic became a public firm on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders.
  • It has been revealed that at the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes.
  • Industry observers note that anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that anthropic became a public firm on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

It has been revealed that at the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

Industry observers note that anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company stated that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”.

With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.

Recent findings suggest that $104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously confirmed $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.

According to recent reports, 28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the firm. Amazon also now has a massive stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab claims.

More than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the organization’s need for future capital is still far greater.

It has been revealed that anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.

Industry observers note that all told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

Industry News: Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Newly introduced York City bill.
  • Industry observers note that I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website.
  • Recent findings suggest that amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Newly introduced York City bill.

Industry observers note that I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website. The message is delivered as a pop-up for consumers of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged into Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.

Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:.

Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.

It has been revealed that it’s not unusual for Amazon to take a stance on political matters, and it has publicly opposed the Delivery Protection Act since April. What is upcoming is Amazon using its online marketplace to push a political view. It’s uncommon to see a pop-up about legislation when visiting a shopping website.

It has been revealed that the messaging suggests that Amazon is concerned about the potential impact the proposed law would have on its costs. Besides Amazon, the bill targets any company with last-mile delivery facilities in NYC, like FedEx and DoorDash.

It has been revealed that it also raises questions about the potential impact on shoppers should Amazon expand its use of its e-commerce platform for additional political messaging. The pop-up launched today impacts only NYC residents but sets a precedent for Amazon to sway political views on other issues. Amazon has made similar moves internally, including reportedly using an app for its employees to campaign against unionizing. But the new pop-up shows Amazon extending that strategy directly to its people.

In a recent development, given Amazon’s considerable influence in commerce, other companies could copy its actions. Uber and Lyft have previously done so, CNBC reports.

Industry observers note that finally, there’s the question of whether Amazon is fairly depicting the situations surrounding the bill. Notable supporters of the Delivery Protection Act include NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Amazon division of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. Using a platform with massive reach to communicate only one side of an ongoing debate could lead to misinformation and a skewed public perception.

It has been revealed that the Delivery Protection Act is at the moment stalled in the City Council’s Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection. The last hearing on the bill was in April. A committee vote on whether to advance the act to the full City Council hasn’t been set.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
  • The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The upcoming program expands on the firm’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which launched in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole newly introduced influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

According to recent reports, first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

Industry observers note that as any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

According to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

It has been revealed that live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

According to recent reports, uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of people — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.

The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting indicates. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”.

The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.”.

TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have released such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the latest John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the firm is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.

Industry observers note that the outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging customers from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”.

Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

Industry observers note that an AI agent from Apple would put the iPhone maker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, Anthropic’s Duet, and Google’s Tasks. Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.

Recent findings suggest that apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps. It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities, as a report from Bloomberg suggests the tech giant could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs. This lines up with the company’s newly introduced job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.

Industry observers note that “People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.”.

With its upcoming iOS 27.3 patch, Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.

A new collapsible sidebar in AI mode shows your most recent searches.

Google is doubling down on Gemini AI in its desktop search, despite protestations from consumers and employees alike. The latest feature is a collapsible sidebar in AI mode that reveals your most recent searches, in case you want to jump back to a previous query. "In testing, this sidebar made a major difference for making progress and continuing to explore the web," wrote VP of search Robby Stein on X.

The fresh sidebar is only available in Google Search's AI mode. Clicking anywhere on the left of the AI search window opens up the sidebar, showing all recent searches, both AI and organic. Then, selecting any of the sidebar descriptions opens up an AI mode search window on the subject. You can close the AI search sidebar at any time by clicking on the "close sidebar" icon at the top right.

New on the Google desktop homepage globally: we're rolling out a collapsible sidebar to easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches.

Recent findings suggest that if you're like me and never use Google's dedicated AI Search mode, you won't see the newly introduced sidebar. Still, it's bound to ruffle some feathers among people and publishers who think there's already too much Gemini in Google Search. (As an, er, sidebar, I'd add that the feature would be nice to have in regular Search, as a list of recent queries would save me from having a zillion tabs open.).

It has been revealed that google seems to value its AI search development more than actual money, given that its market cap recently dropped by $500 billion after it admitted that AI search isn't earning as much as organic search. In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. The launch day for the highly anticipated video game has arrived, more than 13 years after its predecessor.

If you patiently waited more than a decade for GTA 6, you're probably hoping for a long, immersive experience that makes it worth the wait.

In a recent development, good news! Reports are now coming in from game reviewers, and it seems like you're in for a treat. You'll likely be playing GTA 6 for a long time.

Recent findings suggest that an early report from Insider Gaming suggested GTA 6 will take around 50 hours to complete the main campaign. Now that the wider review embargo has lifted, we can get an even more nuanced idea of how long it will take to finish the 91 main story missions GTA 6 has to offer.

For example, our friends at IGN polled four different players who had finished the game, and each of them had something different to say. One player finished the story in "just" 42 hours, which was the lowest estimate. Another took 65 hours, and then a third took 72 hours. Finally, IGN reviewer Luke Reilly said he needed a whopping 115 hours to complete the game.

To be clear, those figures represent the amount of time it took each writer to complete GTA 6's main campaign. If you want to fully complete everything in the game, you're looking at a much longer gameplay time. Much longer.

Sources indicate that aside from GTA 6's main campaign, there are also side quests and an array of interactions, events, and locations to explore. Gamers will likely want to unlock the reported 55 achievements, including the Platinum Trophy and the Mythic achievement.

If you want to do all of that, you could be looking at potentially at least 200 hours of gameplay for GTA 6.

That's not even counting any time spent just wandering the streets of Vice City or cruising around in a car while listening to the stacked GTA 6 soundtrack and radio stations.

In a recent development, so, lock in, gamers (and please take plenty of breaks). More than 200 hours of GTA 6 await. #1969. GTA 6 fans are flying planes into buildings (or trying to)

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (802 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 fans are flying planes into buildings (or trying to)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) debuted on Nov.
  • The Grand Theft Auto series generally revels in grand theft auto, grand theft aerial, and wanton urban destruction.
  • Sources indicate that in GTA 6's predecessor GTA 5, ramming an aircraft into a building would damage the plane and often cause it to explode, with Los Santos' indestructible highrises left intact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) debuted on Nov. 19, prompting gamers everywhere to take the day off and indulge in a lawless land of hedonism and crime. Unsurprisingly, one of the first activities some people tried in the open world sandbox game was to fly a plane into a building. However, these antics haven't been producing the results many expected.

The Grand Theft Auto series generally revels in grand theft auto, grand theft aerial, and wanton urban destruction. Even so, there is particular sensitivity around the subject of crashing planes into buildings. The 9/11 attacks 25 years ago remain a pivotal moment in the U.S. consciousness, to such an extent that many people's minds immediately venture there when presented with a plane and a building.

Sources indicate that in GTA 6's predecessor GTA 5, ramming an aircraft into a building would damage the plane and often cause it to explode, with Los Santos' indestructible highrises left intact. Previous Grand Theft Auto games also didn't allow planes to damage buildings. Nevertheless, some fans wondered if GTA 6 would skew this trend, particularly as it aims to feel realistic.

In a recent development, according to early gameplay clips, this doesn't seem to be the case. In a widely circulated clip by Twitch streamer Windpress, his character parachutes from a plane aimed at a building, only to watch the aircraft apparently pass harmlessly through it. Another popular GTA 6 gameplay video from @DiegoPalmaX revealed a manned plane collide with a building but remain completely intact, slowly falling to the ground and even hitting another structure on the way down.

Such clips have drawn criticism from some Grand Theft Auto fans, who have commented on the lack of realism.

"you can't commit 9/11 in gta 6…" wrote X user @eveisthebastard. "'realism' smh…".

"people will undoubtably say stuff like this doesnt really matter and i would usually agree but when literally all the hype for this game has been 'wow look at all the details there are ten trillion things being simulated' then yeah it really does matter," stated @fbq_2.

Meanwhile, others have argued that it's reasonable for developer Rockstar Games to prevent players from recreating the 9/11 attacks.

"[The point of the game] is to commit crimes. Not be a terrorist," wrote @_MiisterJ. "Why would a game let you recreate 9/11?... Out of everything the game has to offer you draw the line at doing 9/11??".

Sources indicate that some have suggested that GTA 6's unusual interactions between planes and buildings may be the result of bugs. Launch day bugs are common in upcoming video games, with developers often issuing patches to fix them later on. Considering the strange behaviour of GTA 6's planes, particularly when compared to GTA 5, the idea that these are errors seems like a reasonable theory.

However, other social media customers have attributed the viral videos of pristine planes to a toggle in GTA 6's settings. Found under gameplay settings, GTA 6 includes a Reduced Vehicle Damage toggle which increases the amount of abuse your car or plane can take. Though it hasn't been confirmed that this setting was responsible for the nonsensical plane-building interactions seen in widely spread GTA 6 clips, activating it could theoretically help prevent vehicles from becoming deadly fireballs.

According to recent reports, further GTA 6 gameplay videos have supported suggestions that the viral clips are unusual by capturing more typically expected interactions between buildings and planes. A clip from Twitch streamer ohnePixel reveals his small plane exploding after he flies it into a building, though like in GTA 5 the building itself remains undamaged. Another video shared on X by @muaxh03 shows a plane being destroyed after its left wing hits a building, killing the player character.

Industry observers note that in an interview with Love magazine, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson stated that GTA 6 attempts to balance realism with immersion, indicating that it may deviate where strict adherence to reality would make the game less fun. Whether this includes declining to realistically depict what happens when a jet flies into a highrise will likely become clearer as more people jump in to play. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that buzz buzz, Yellowjackets hive! Season 4 is upon us, and we're ready to be dragged back into the creepy woods of teen chaos and middle-aged mayhem. The Season 3 finale offered some major moments, including the revelation of the Pit Girl's identity and Natalie (Sophie Thatcher) sending out a distress call to the civilized world.

Recent findings suggest that trailers for Season 4 have teased the titular soccer team's return home. However, if the first three seasons have taught us anything, it's that you can take the girl out of the wilderness, but you can't take the wilderness out of the girl. In both the past and present timelines, Shauna (Sophie Nélisse/Melanie Lynskey), Misty (Samantha Hanratty/Christina Ricci), and Taissa (Jasmin Savoy Brown/Tawny Cypress) are grappling for survival and control, so buckle up for a wild ride.

But hey, if the off-season has you feeling foggy on which teammates (and rivals) have bit the dust (or been bit up), we've got you covered with a recap of all the deaths in Seasons 1, 2, and 3.

And keep an eye on this space — the final season of Yellowjackets is sure to see more folks fall, and we'll be updating this list accordingly.

In a recent development, also, wherever possible, we have images with sliders of before and after. Slide 'em if you can stomach it.

Having just moved up from the junior varsity team, Rachel has the grim distinction of being the first Yellowjacket to die. Like the plane's pilots, she died in the crash, from a laceration to her throat.

Father of Travis and Javi, Coach Bill (Carlos Sanz) died as a result of the plane crash that dropped the team in the Canadian wilderness. He'd fallen out of the plane into a tree. In an added bit of brutality, he died in front of Travis, as the teen boy tried to save him from his painful perch in a tree.

It has been revealed that good Christian girl Laura Lee (Jane Widdop) died a hero. After the team found an intact plane in the wilderness, Laura Lee began reading the manual to figure out how to fly it. She eventually took off with her teddy bear Leonard — and her personal lord and savior Jesus — as her co-pilots. But the plane exploded in the air, killing Laura and the Yellowjackets' chance of sending out a member for help.

The queen bee who couldn't hack it in the cabin, Jackie (Ella Purnell) froze to death while sleeping outside. And then she had the bizarre honor of becoming the first to be eaten by the team.

Travis's younger brother Javi (Luciano Leroux) would also be eaten, though the Yellowjackets weren't directly to blame for his death. While the team was hunting Natalie, Javi offered her a hiding place. But before they could get to safety, he fell through the ice of a frozen lake and died. From there, he was eaten.

In a recent development, despite the best efforts of the team, Shauna's baby was stillborn. This was a sad one.

Remember when Misty made a friend? She and Kristen (who was dubbed Crystal the Pistol by the team) bonded in the wilderness over their shared love of music and Steel Magnolias. They grew close enough that Misty shared her secret about destroying the plane's emergency transmitter, which Kristen — understandably — judged. From there, Misty pushed her off a cliff, and proclaimed the girl "missing.".

Real talk: Ben (Steven Krueger) lived way longer than we expected. The plane crash severely damaged his leg, which Misty then amputated on the spot. And incredibly, he survived possible infection, likely starvation, and the burning down of the cabin. But he couldn't escape the Yellowjackets. In a kangaroo court, they convicted him for the cabin's fiery annihilation (despite Misty's best efforts of a defense), and Taissa was chosen to carry out the execution. However, this was not how Ben died. Instead, he was tortured with crippling violence and deplorable conditions — that is, until Natalie took mercy on him and stabbed him fatally in the heart.

Poor Edwin (Nelson Franklin) just wanted to study frogs with his colleague Hannah (Ashley Sutton) and their guide Kodiak (Joel McHale). But then he stumbled in the Yellowjackets camp as they were feasting on Ben's remains. And, well, Lottie welcomed him with an axe to the head. RIP Edwin.

In a recent development, after Edwin was killed, the Yellowjackets imprisoned his surviving friends like they did Ben. When Kodiak tried to escape, he wasn't ended by the girls but by Hannah, who stabbed him in the eye. This was Hannah's bid to show the girls she could be trusted to keep their secret. And it got her through the rest of Season 3 at least.

Yellowjackets began — to quote Sarah McLachlan — building a mystery by introducing the show with the death of the Pit Girl. Underdressed for the snowy weather, she raced through the woods, pursued by masked figures, and ultimately fell into a pit of spikes, which killed her. Season 3 revealed her identity: Mari Ibarra (Alexa Barajas), a persistent rival of Shauna's. Mari too was eaten.

It has been revealed that how Travis (Andres Soto) died was a big mystery in Season 1, with a real bummer of a reveal. In the present, accidentally hanged himself while attempting to talk to the darkness. Lottie was supposed to save him but had a technical malfunction.

In a recent development, in Season 1, Adam Martin (Peter Gadiot) was a mechanic who was having an affair with Shauna. But when Shauna began to suspect he had betrayed her, she stabbed him to death. His murder was covered up with the help of Misty, Nat, Taissa, and Jeff, because Yellowjackets are ride or die. (Sometimes both!).

Masquerading as a journalist, Jessica Roberts (Rekha Sharma) got on the wrong side of Misty Quigley, who fatally poisoned her with fentanyl-laced cigarettes.

Taisaa's family pet was murdered by Night Taissa. Then, his head was placed on creepy basement altar, which would prove a foreshadowing for Ben's fate.

In Season 2, Detective Kevyn Tan (Alex Wyndham) was put in the awkward position of investigating his former high school classmates as he looked into the disappearance of Adam Martin. When his search led him to Lottie's cult's headquarters, he was felled — not by a Yellowjacket! — but by one of their fans. Specifically, Walter Tattersall (Elijah Wood), a citizen detective who fell for Misty. As the two were talking, Walter subtly poisoned Kevyn with a laced hot cocoa.

Nat (Juliette Lewis) died in the Season 2 finale, and we're still not over it. Of all the survivors, she seemed the one who likely to succeed in escaping their past. Worse yet, she was killed by her friend, Misty.

It was an accident. Misty was trying to kill one of Lottie's cult members, Lisa (Nicole Maines), but Nat intervened by throwing her own body in front of the syringe, which was filled with poison. However, Natalie's story continued in the flashbacks. And yet, that only promised to make her ending sadder.

It has been revealed that who killed Lottie Matthews (Simone Kessell)? Well, to the surprise of many, it wasn't Shauna. It was her daughter, Callie Sadecki (Sarah Desjardins). Sure, Callie and Lottie had bonded, no matter how much that enraged Shauna. But when Callie confronted Lottie about stealing the incriminating DAT tape from the Sadecki home, Lottie began saying cryptic things about how Callie was a child of the Wilderness' darkness. In a rage, Callie reacted by shoving Lottie down the stairs.

Recent findings suggest that taissa's high school paramour (Liv Hewson) rejoined to the fold to reignite their romance and proved a solid teammate (Lauren Ambrose) in the present timeline. But their bliss was punctured by Van's cancer diagnosis, and yet that was not how she died! Hopeful the whatever of the wilderness would save her if she sacrificed someone else, Van tried to kill Melissa (Hilary Swank), a ball-capped Yellowjacket who was long thought dead, but had resurfaced under weird circumstances.

According to recent reports, ultimately, however, Van decided not kill Melissa. And in response, Melissa fatally stabbed her and fled, leaving Taissa to bury Van in an unmarked grave. Naturally, she took the opportunity to cut her lover open and eat her heart.

Whats new to streaming this week? (Nov. 20, 2026)
